title: Show-all page lists every published report with likes, visible comments and times opened, counting opens once per visitor per day and ignoring bots
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

C2: The list is newest first: missing
C3: Each row shows the title and published-on date: missing

visible-comment-count-four-way-agreement: B (110-chain): SQL=Tree=printed=110 but page draws 5 (cap here is 5, not 100); A, C, D agree

Where opens live. Practice puts them in internal/votes (opens.go) to inherit the no-transaction fence. Crossdomain uses a new internal/opens package with its own fences. I chose internal/opens to match the one-fenced-package-per-table model.

The visitor key. Practice uses a random in-memory key, and a restart re-counts that day. Crossdomain derives the key from HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, so it is stable across restarts, and redacts it at day close. I chose in-memory; the derived key without redaction would leave stored rows reversible.

Row wording and side. Practice uses labels first: 'Likes N', 'Comments N', 'Times opened N'. Crossdomain uses numbers first: 'N likes', 'N comments', 'N views'. I chose numbers first because 'N comments' is the measured format. The column therefore reads 'views', not the slice's 'times opened'. A person may prefer the slice's words, which means going back to labels first.
Whether the signed-in owner's opens count. Practice excludes them and crossdomain counts them. I excluded them.
Practice's Sec-Purpose/Purpose prefetch skip. I dropped it.
IPv6 grouping by /64. Practice has it and crossdomain does not. I kept it.
How an unparsable X-Forwarded-For entry resolves. Practice does not count it; crossdomain falls back to the nearest valid hop. I chose not counting.
How misconfiguration is reported. Practice warns once at runtime; crossdomain logs at startup when the list is empty. I chose the runtime warning, which also catches a wrong proxy address.

critique missed: M2's prescribed fix (one checker script, tests/acceptance/run_finish.py, running every ledger body) never asked what a body does when its browser launch falls back to msedge. Q-028 was already open and recorded that e004_2's ledger body hard-codes an msedge path and ignores CHROME_BIN. The first script keyed its Edge guard on CHROME_BIN and carried a hard-coded Chrome install path. Code-review #1 measured that with CHROME_BIN unset the script ran a body naming msedge. A usable check would grep the 12 baseline bodies for 'msedge' and for browser paths before prescribing a runner that executes them.

critique missed: M1's prescribed fix (a trusted peer with no untrusted client entry is not counted, plus a warning), and the critic's extension to an inner-hop-only list, still left the shipped default silent. With HBAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES unset, an untrusted internal peer (the proxy) that sends no X-Forwarded-For is returned as the client with no log line, which is the same R-004 collapse M1 was filed for. The critique never ran the check 'with the variable unset and no XFF, does anything get logged?', which lesson #929 says to ask of every shipped default. It was waived afterwards (O-031, N-159).

critique missed: m2's prescribed fix replaced a five-name list with shape patterns for client-identity header names, but nobody ran the patterns against a real real-IP library's header list. They stayed quiet on "X-Forwarded", "Cf-Pseudo-IPv4" and "CF-Connecting-IPv6", in either quote style. This is the same class closed once and reopened, now carried to SC-040. A usable check is a fire row for each header in request-ip's list before accepting the patterns.

Fix exactly these with the smallest change: one scoped re-check reads only your fix. Sent back with what raised them: O-026 (fix): m1 (minor): run_body is meant to never run a finish body that would start Edge, but its guard tests the wrong file. test_e004_2's body picks the first browser in its own list that exists: its own hard-coded Chrome path, then msedge. The guard only asks whether the file in CHROME_BIN exists, falling back to the hard-coded CHROME constant on line 67. So on a machine where CHROME_BIN names a Chrome anywhere other than the body's own path, the guard passes and the body starts msedge, which this machine forbids. The script also writes a browser install path into code (line 67) and falls back to it when CHROME_BIN is unset. The engine's standing rule names both as defects. On this PC CHROME_BIN equals the standard path, so today's runs started Chrome. Skip a body that names msedge unless the Chrome path that body itself looks for exists. Parse that path out of the body, and skip when none can be found. Drop the CHROME constant and the `or CHROME` fallback. [shown by a failing run] The engine ran the code review's test for this, tests/acceptance/test_run_finish_edge_guard.py, with `python -I tests/acceptance/test_run_finish_edge_guard.py`, and it FAILED. Put that test at tests/acceptance/test_run_finish_edge_guard.py as it is -- comments and layout aside -- and make it pass. The engine runs `python -I tests/acceptance/test_run_finish_edge_guard.py` again in your tree, and that run is what closes this; your word does not. The test: """run_finish.py must never run a finish body that would start Edge. test_e004_2's body opens the first browser of its own list that exists: its own Chrome path, then msedge. Whether CHROME_BIN names a Chrome somewhere else says nothing about which of the two the body will take, so a body that names msedge must not be run on the strength of CHROME_BIN alone. When CHROME_BIN is unset it uses that path in its place (`os.environ.get("CHROME_BIN") or CHROME`). The guard that is meant to stop a finish body from falling back to Edge also checks the wrong thing. It asks whether CHROME_BIN's file exists. The e004_2 ledger body ignores CHROME_BIN (Q-028) and picks from its own candidate list, which names msedge. So when CHROME_BIN points at a Chrome that is not on the body's list, the guard passes and the body falls back to msedge. That starts Edge, which must never be started on this machine. Measured: with CHROME_BIN unset, run_body ran a body that names msedge. Delete the CHROME constant and take the browser from CHROME_BIN only: `chrome = os.environ.get("CHROME_BIN"); if "msedge" in body and not (chrome and os.path.isfile(chrome)): return None, 0.0, "skipped: CHROME_BIN is unset ..."` Better still, skip any body that names msedge unless CHROME_BIN is the first browser on that body's own list.
